editorial:
Ever wondered what it is actually like to hang out with people who believe the Earth is flat? You get a front-row seat to that world here. Instead of making fun of these folks, the movie takes a weirdly kind approach. You follow a few main characters who are totally convinced that the globe is a lie and that we are living on a giant pancake. It feels less like a science lesson and more like a character study. You will see how they find community in a world that mostly laughs at them, and the vibe is surprisingly human and awkward at the same time.

What really makes this work is the pacing. It does not drag, and it keeps you guessing about where these people are going with their logic. The best part is seeing them actually try to prove their points with real experiments. If you enjoy seeing people stumble upon the truth in the most confusing way possible, you will love this. You can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video for the best picture, or just rent it on Apple TV for a quick movie night. It is a great pick for a group hangout where you can argue about the plot afterward.
endingExplained: The big climax happens when one of the characters performs an experiment using a flashlight and a level to prove the Earth is curved. Even though the results clearly show the curve, he refuses to believe the evidence. He makes up a new excuse to explain why the test failed instead of admitting he was wrong. It shows you that no matter how much proof you have, some people will never change their minds.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves social experiments and strange human behavior.
